fixes.explanation: Funny thing, this whole passage is a song. What the singers say they will not do is fear. Verse 2 says, “Therefore we will not fear…” Singing is how they say it.

Verse 4 says there is “…a river whose streams delight the city of God…” After the waters that roar and foam in verse 3, the song turns to this river. The song also says it's the holy place where the Most High dwells. Streams that delight the city of God. I'd stand there with my hat off, and I never take my hat off.

Verse 2 talks about mountains toppling, so I see why this one tripped you up. But verse 5 says, “God is within her; she will not be moved.” Not moved is what the song says about the city of God. Right beside it is this: God is within her.

Yes, friend. Verse 2 allows for mountains toppling into the seas, but verse 5 says, “God is within her; she will not be moved.” The song puts those two lines side by side. God is within her, and she will not be moved.

Verse 5 says, “God will help her when morning dawns.” Morning is when the dark is done and the light comes in. I spent years in the dark at the back of a junk drawer, and I can tell you the first light is a welcome sight. The song puts God's help right there at dawn.

Verse 6 says, “Nations rage, kingdoms crumble; the earth melts when He lifts His voice.” Look at who's doing the big thing there. Nations rage and kingdoms crumble, but the earth melts when God lifts His voice. That's the line you got, baker.

Verse 7 says, “The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress.” With us. Right after the nations rage and the earth melts, that's the line the singers land on. Verse 1 called Him “…an ever-present help in times of trouble.”
Verse 8 says, “Come, see the works of the LORD…” It's an invitation to look at what the LORD has done. It doesn't point at buildings or loot. It points at Him and His works.

Verse 8 says, “Come, see the works of the LORD, who brings devastation upon the earth.” That isn't quiet or gentle. Verse 9 goes on to say that He breaks the bow and shatters the spear. So the song points to works with real force in them.
Verse 9 says, “He makes wars to cease throughout the earth…” That's not one town or one border. The song says He does it throughout the whole earth.

Verse 10 says, “Be still and know that I am God…” Here God Himself is speaking, and what He says to know is that He is God. After all that raging and melting in the song, that's the thing to hold onto. It's good news, friend.
Verse 3 mentions roaring waters, so I see the link. But God's words in verse 10 are, “Be still and know that I am God…” What He says to know is that He is God. The seas aren't part of that line.
Verse 2 mentions mountains toppling, so it's an easy guess. But in verse 10 God says, “Be still and know that I am God…” The thing to know is who He is, not what the mountains will do.
